text:
Ivy Chen: Quick thread — onboarding + CI pain. We have three places users stash creds: REDWOOD_API_KEY, CLI token file (~/.redwood/token), and Kubernetes secrets. But SDKs behave inconsistently and Docker sample images often fail in CI because they rely on env-only. Can we standardize and document best practices?

Omar Rizvi: Saw 2 tickets where CI builds used REDWOOD_API_KEY in GitHub Actions but local dev used `redwood login`. Build containers didn't mount ~/.redwood so tests 401ed.

Priya Kumar: Minimal spec idea: precedence order by default: 1) explicit client creds passed in code (highest), 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY env, 3) REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN env (scoped), 4) token file path REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE (default ~/.redwood/token), 5) container- or OS-level secret providers (keychain, k8s file). Allow override via CredentialProvider.order.

Ben Torres: Add: SDKs should expose client.metadata.auth_source = 'env'|'file'|'k8s' so sample apps and telemetry can report which source used (masked). Also mask tokens in logs and never dump full key.

Ivy Chen: Rotation flow: gateway sends 401 with header `x-rw-auth-status: expired` or `x-rw-auth-status: revoked`. SDK behavior: on expired -> if there is a lower-priority source, try it once; if none, emit `auth:expired` event and raise a friendly error with next steps (re-login, set REDWOOD_API_KEY). On revoked -> fail fast with `credentials-revoked` message.

Omar Rizvi: CI nuance: ephemeral tokens injected via GH Actions should prefer env and not fallback to file. Suggest we add an option `preferEnvInCI` that detects CI env var and disables file fallback to avoid leaking or confusing credentials.

Priya Kumar: Good call. For Docker/devcontainer quickstarts, update README snippets to show both options: mounting ~/.redwood or setting REDWOOD_API_KEY. Add `redwood whoami --json` that prints {org, project, auth_source} so CI logs can assert auth_source=="env" in tests.

Ben Torres: Security note: telemetry about fallback should be opt-in and only send auth_source enum, never secret material. Also add an SDK config `logAuthSource: true` default false in prod.

Ivy Chen: For SDK API, propose small provider interface: get(), refreshIfNeeded(), sources() -> array. Keep sync and async variants. Example: ```js
const prov = new CredentialProvider({order:['env','file','k8s'], preferEnvInCI:true})
const client = new Redwood({credentials: prov, refreshOn401:true})
console.log('auth_source=', client.metadata.auth_source)
```

Omar Rizvi: Tests: unit test precedence, e2e with auth stub returning `x-rw-auth-status: expired` and assert provider tries fallback then emits event. Also test container image with no token file.

Priya Kumar: I'll draft the short spec and quickstart copy. We should also add a migration note in console login: "If you're using containers or CI, prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY or set REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE mount."

cred-bot: Created ticket RDW-9456: "Auth provider parity: precedence, CI behavior, whoami, rotation semantics" assigned to @Ben Torres.

Ben Torres: Taking RDW-9456. I'll open PR for node SDK provider + sample updates this week, then follow-up for python. Thanks all.
